items.item_text: Current BLS certificate from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross
Bachelor’s of Science in Nursing (BSN) or Master’s of Science in nursing (MSN)
Minimum 1 year of clinical experience in an acute psychiatric setting
Experience caring for patients and families experiencing mental/ behavior health issues
Minimum 2 years of experience in a psychiatric or behavioral health setting

At UCLA, our Perinatal Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) provides specialized psychiatric care and evidence-based treatment for individuals experiencing maternal health conditions during pregnancy and the postpartum period. As part of a collaborative multidisciplinary team, you will care for patients participating in treatment alongside their infants, helping families navigate recovery while supporting maternal-infant boding and overall well-being. You will play a vital role in delivering high-quality patient care while supporting positive clinical outcomes and exceptional experiences. Key responsibilities:
Assess, plan, implement, and evaluate individualized patient care
Perform comprehensive patient assessments and document clinical findings
Administer medications, treatments, and therapeutic interventions in accordance with physician orders and nursing standards
Collaborate with physicians and interdisciplinary team members to coordinate care and support treatment goals
Educate patients and their families regarding treatment plans, health conditions, and ongoing care needs
Promote a safe, therapeutic, and patient-centered treatment environment
Participate in quality improvement, evidence-based practice, and professional development activities
Ability to safely lift and carry infants up to one year of age and remain active within the therapeutic milieu throughout the shift
